raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`rid` is the correlation key that ties a request together across the TokenizerManager, scheduler and detokenizer logs. For generate requests a caller can already supply their own — `GenerateReqInput._normalize_rid` accepts a single `str` and expands it into per-item rids:

```python
elif isinstance(self.rid, str):
    new_rids = [f"{self.rid}_{i}" for i in range(num)]
    self.rid = new_rids
```

There is no equivalent for the Score API. `Engine.score()` / `async_score()` / `TokenizerManager.score_request()` expose no `rid` parameter, so scoring traffic always gets auto-generated ids. When a scoring request misbehaves (slow, retried, or dropped) there is no way to line the sglang-side logs up with the caller's own request id, which makes debugging in a service that fronts sglang considerably harder.

The underlying `EmbeddingReqInput` also could not accept a base rid: its batch path asserted the rid was already a list.

## Modifications

- Add an optional `rid: Optional[str] = None` to `Engine.score()`, `Engine.async_score()` and `TokenizerManager.score_request()`, threaded down to the `GenerateReqInput` / `EmbeddingReqInput` that scoring builds.
- Teach `EmbeddingReqInput.normalize_batch_and_arguments` to expand a single `str` rid into `<rid>_<i>` for a batch, mirroring `GenerateReqInput._normalize_rid`. The previous `assert isinstance(self.rid, list)` now only applies to the non-str case.

A scoring call fans out into one sub-request per item, which is why the base id is expanded rather than reused verbatim — reusing it would produce duplicate rids and trip `_validate_rid_uniqueness`.

Default behavior is unchanged: `rid=None` still auto-generates, and existing callers that pass a list still work.

## Accuracy Tests

Purely additive — no change to scoring math or to any existing code path when `rid` is not supplied. Added unit tests to `test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py` (registered CPU suite) covering rid normalization on `EmbeddingReqInput`: single (non-batch) str preserved, str expanded to `<rid>_<i>` across a batch, `None` auto-generates unique per-item ids, and an explicit list passes through untouched.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable — no change on the hot path; this only affects how the request id is chosen.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation-running-docs-ci).
- [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/accuracy_evaluation.html).
- [x] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR.
- [x] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.ai to discuss your PR.

nodes.body:
Rebased onto current `main` and fixed a collision hazard found in self-review.

The scheduler aborts by **prefix** match (`req.rid.startswith(recv_req.rid)`) across the waiting queue, running batch, chunked request and every disaggregation queue. Auto-generated rids are fixed-length `uuid4().hex`, so no rid can prefix another — but expanding a caller-supplied base rid as `f"{rid}_{i}"` broke that invariant. For a batch of ≥11, `base_1` prefixes `base_10`, so aborting one item (client disconnect, or one item failing validation) silently aborted its siblings. The score API is exactly the high-fan-out case where this is routine.

Changes:
- Expansion zero-pads the index to a fixed width, via a shared `expand_base_rid()` used by both `GenerateReqInput._normalize_rid` and `EmbeddingReqInput`.
- That helper rejects empty/non-str rids and rids starting with the reserved `HEALTH_CHECK` / `draft:` prefixes, which change scheduler control flow — a `HEALTH_CHECK`-prefixed request is dropped when the scheduler isn't idle and `_handle_abort_req` returns early for it, so the caller would wait forever.
- `_init_req_state` now checks all rids before inserting any. It raised mid-loop on a duplicate but is called outside the caller's `try/except`, so earlier insertions leaked with no waiter and no remover, permanently poisoning those rids.
Superseded by #44152, which consolidates related changes into one PR for easier review. Closing in favor of that one.

 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
+# Reserved rid prefixes that change scheduler control flow rather than just
+# labelling a request, so a caller-supplied rid must never start with them.
+_RESERVED_RID_PREFIXES = (HEALTH_CHECK_RID_PREFIX, "draft:")
+
+
+def expand_base_rid(rid: str, num: int) -> List[str]:
+    """Expand one caller-supplied base rid into ``num`` per-item rids.
+
+    The index is zero-padded to a fixed width because the scheduler matches rids
+    by *prefix* when aborting (``req.rid.startswith(recv_req.rid)``). With an
+    unpadded index ``<base>_1`` is a prefix of ``<base>_10``, so aborting a single
+    item of a batch of 11 or more would silently abort its siblings too.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(rid, str) or not rid:
+        raise ValueError("The rid should be a non-empty string.")
+    for reserved in _RESERVED_RID_PREFIXES:
+        if rid.startswith(reserved):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"The rid must not start with the reserved prefix {reserved!r}."
+            )
+    width = len(str(num - 1)) if num > 1 else 1
+    return [f"{rid}_{i:0{width}d}" for i in range(num)]
+

+class TestEmbeddingReqInputRidNormalization(CustomTestCase):
+    """Test rid normalization in EmbeddingReqInput.normalize_batch_and_arguments."""
+
+    def test_single_str_rid_is_preserved(self):
+        req = EmbeddingReqInput(text="Hello", rid="my-rid")
+        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()

+

+        """One base rid fans out to per-item rids, like GenerateReqInput."""
+        req = EmbeddingReqInput(text=["Hello", "World", "!"], rid="my-rid")
+        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()

+

+        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
+        self.assertEqual(len(req.rid), 2)

+
+    def test_list_rid_is_passed_through(self):
+        req = EmbeddingReqInput(text=["Hello", "World"], rid=["a", "b"])
+        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
+        self.assertEqual(req.rid, ["a", "b"])

+        """The scheduler aborts by prefix match, so no sub-rid may prefix another.

+        With an unpadded index ``base_1`` prefixes ``base_10``, so aborting one
+        item of a >=11 item score call would silently abort its siblings.

+        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()

+        self.assertEqual(req.rid[11], "base_11")
+        for a in req.rid:
+            for b in req.rid:
+                if a is not b:
+                    self.assertFalse(b.startswith(a), f"{a!r} prefixes {b!r}")
+
+    def test_expanded_rids_unpadded_for_small_batches(self):
+        req = EmbeddingReqInput(text=["Hello", "World", "!"], rid="my-rid")
+        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
+        self.assertEqual(req.rid, ["my-rid_0", "my-rid_1", "my-rid_2"])
+
+    def test_reserved_rid_prefix_rejected(self):
+        for bad in ("HEALTH_CHECK", "HEALTH_CHECK-1", "draft:abc"):
+            with self.subTest(rid=bad):
+                req = EmbeddingReqInput(text=["a", "b"], rid=bad)
+                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "reserved prefix"):
+                    req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
+
+    def test_empty_rid_rejected(self):
+        req = EmbeddingReqInput(text=["a", "b"], rid="")
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "non-empty string"):
+            req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
+
+    def test_generate_req_input_expansion_is_also_padded(self):
+        req = GenerateReqInput(text=["x"] * 12, rid="base")
+        req.normalize_batch_and_arguments()
+        self.assertEqual(req.rid[0], "base_00")
+        self.assertEqual(req.rid[11], "base_11")
+
+
